scenes.imageLabel: Clear sky · Punjab and Haryana · 3 Nov 2023
scenes.question: If you test 751 cells, how many look special by luck?

beats.say: Flip a fair coin five times, and getting all heads is rare. But give a coin to a thousand people, and a few of them will get five heads just by luck. Test enough things, and some will always look special. That is not magic; it is just how chance works.

Test a trend in 751 cells at the five percent level, and about 38 will look significant by chance alone. Formula thirty-seven, the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate, controls the share of false discoveries among the cells it marks, so a trend map does not light up with noise.

parts.say: First, sort all m p-values from smallest to largest. The small brackets mean their position in the sorted list.

Then walk up the list. Each p-value gets its own bar: i over m, times alpha, the target false discovery rate. The first p-value must beat a very strict bar, and later ones a gentler bar. k is the last position where a p-value still sits under its bar.
Finally, every test up to position k is called a discovery. Among those marked cells, the expected share of false alarms is at most alpha.

steps.label: Cells tested
steps.say: In Punjab and Haryana, FIREWORK ran Mann-Kendall on the October and November cell-days of every cell with enough fires: 751 cells.

steps.label: Cells with p below 0.05
steps.say: Of those, 446 have a p-value below 0.05. About 38 of them would do that by chance.

steps.label: Survive FDR at 5%
steps.say: After the Benjamini-Hochberg rule, 387 cells survive: 375 falling and 12 rising. So the decline in residue burning is real across most of the agricultural plain, not a few lucky cells.

beats.say: On the left, the sorted p-values, climbing from left to right, with the Benjamini-Hochberg line, i over m times 0.05. Everything below the last crossing is a discovery.
On the right, the cells with a significant trend after this control, coloured by direction. The falling cells cover most of the farm belt.

beats.label: The formula, numbered F37
beats.say: On the FIREWORK website, this method lives in the Formulas section. Its page shows the equation, numbered as formula 37, with every symbol explained.

beats.label: Where it comes from · why · how · example
beats.say: Below it, four short cards explain where the method comes from, why FIREWORK needs it, how it works step by step, and a worked example. The full derivation is in the PDF on the same page.

points: Sort p-values; compare each with (i/m) · α
Controls the share of false discoveries among marked cells

beats.say: So, to remember: when you test many cells at once, some will look special by luck. The step-up rule keeps the share of false alarms among marked cells small, so a coloured cell can be trusted.
